rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING MINING ROYALTIES TO GOVERNMENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES, ESTABLISHING MECHANISMS FOR ITS PROPER PAYMENT, COLLECTION AND ADMINISTRATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"State's Royalty Act of 2005.\" The bill proposes to charge mineral resources extractors a mining royalty equivalent to 12% of the net sales profit of the mineral resources extractor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2005-02-21

rows.author: D050
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING MINING ROYALTIES TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLE AND OTHER COMMUNITIES AFFECTED BY MINING OPERATIONS AND ANY OTHER ACTIVITY ARISING FROM THE EXPLORATION, UTILIZATION, EXTRACTION AND DEVELOPMENT OF ANY MINERAL RESOURCE FROM ANY MASS OF LAND OR PROPERTY INCLUDING BODIES OF WATER AND ANY NATURAL RESOURCE THAT THESE PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES OWN, OCCUPY AND UTILIZE FOR THEIR SOCIAL, ECONOMIC, CULTURAL AND COMMON WELFARE, ESTABLISHING MECHANISMS FOR ITS PROPER PAYMENT, COLLECTION AND ADMINISTRATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Mining Profits Withholding Act of 2005.\" The bill prescribes the rules to be observed in the repatriation of the profits and capital of foreign mining companies. It prescribes the mining royalty rates to be granted to indigenous people and other communities affected by mining operations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2005-02-21

rows.author: A041
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING 50% OF PROFITS AND CAPITAL BY MINING COMPANIES OPERATING IN THE PHILIPPINES TO BE RETAINED IN GOVERNMENT BANKS FOR A MINIMUM PERIOD OF TWENTY-FIVE (25) YEARS, ESTABLISHING MECHANISMS FOR ITS PROPER RETENTION AND ADMINISTRATION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Mining Profits Withholdings Act of 2005.\" The bill presrcibes the rules that shall govern the repatriation of profits and capital by foreign mining companies.

rows.mother_status: Unfinished Business (Period of Interpellation)
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MAGNA CARTA FOR WOMEN
rows.abstract: \"The Magna Carta for Women.\" The bill seeks to address the wide-ranging needs and sectoral concerns of women, specially those in the marginalized sector.  It concretizes women's participation and empowerment in all aspects of the family, community and society.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05285

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE ACT OF TERRORISM AS HEINOUS CRIME AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFORE
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Terrorism Act of 2005.\" The bill seeks to define terrorist activities and imposes the penalty of death on those found guilty of committing terrorism.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04839

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NATIONAL IDENTIFICATION  SYSTEM, DEFINING ITS COVERAGE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The measure establishes a national identification system (NIS). The NIS shall preserve national security and expedite private and public transactions.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2006-09-13

committee_action.action: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2006-09-13

rows.author: D007
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO CREATE A LOCAL HOUSING BOARD IN EVERY CITY AND MUNICIPALITY, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND DEFINING ITS DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Local Housing Board Act.\" The bill mandates the creation of the Local Housing Board (LHB) in every city and first to third class municipality to formulate, implement and monitor policies on the provision of housing and on the observance of a just and humane procedure in cases of eviction and demolition. Mandates local government units to allocate 1% of their internal revenue allotment for the activities of the LHB.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2005-05-10, transmitted to on 2005-05-11 and received by the Senate on 2005-05-17

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to insert the Explanatory Note as the sponsorship remarks of the measure. Approved on Second Reading with amendments.

rows.abstract: The bill mandates the conduct of yearly monitoring and inspection of the security and safety facilities, features and equipment in all domestic airports nationwide.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-02-23

rows.title_short: \"Responsible Parenthood and Population Management Act of 2005.\"
rows.abstract: \"Responsible Parenthood and Population Management Act of 2005.\" The bill sets in place a national policy that assures adequate and continuing information on reproductive health and a full range of family planning methods (excluding abortion).
rows.status: Unfinished Business (Period of Sponsorship)

rows.abstract: The measure seeks to declare the tamarraw, which can only be found in the Philippines, as the national mammal.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2002-02-28

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 3 (B) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 3518, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7169, ENTITLED \"AN ACT CREATING THE PHILIPPINE VETERANS BANK AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill limits the ownership of shares of stock in the Veterans Bank to 1,000 shares per veteran, widow or compulsory heir. It also proposes to extend ownership of the Bank's stocks to veterans other than World War II veterans.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2002-02-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO IMPROVE EFFICIENCY IN THE DELIVERY OF GOVERNMENT SERVICE TO THE PUBLIC BY REDUCING BUREAUCRATIC RED TAPE, PREVENTING GRAFT AND CORRUPTION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Red Tape Act of 2005.\" The bill defines certain terms such as simple and complex transactions, frontline services, fixers, action and irrelevant requirements. It provides for clear administrative guidelines and procedures in accessing frontline services.
rows.status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09485) enacted on 2007-06-02
rows.remarks: On Feb. 20, 2007, House concurred with its Senate version (SB02589).

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING CYBERCRIME, PROVIDING FOR PREVENTION, SUPPRESSION AND IMPOSITION OF PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2005.\" The bill seeks to define cybercrime, identify punishable acts involving computers, provide penalties, determine legal procedures for the investigation and prosecution of cybercrimes, clarify jurisdiction and provide for a clause on mutual assistance and cooperation. It provides for the creation of the Cyber-Crime Investigation and Coordination Center.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2002-02-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL GOVERNMENT CORPORATIONS TO PREPARE THEIR RESPECTIVE ASSET AND LIABILITY MANAGEMENT GUIDELINES THAT WILL DEFINE THE PARAMETERS AND/OR LIMITS OF THEIR FINANCIAL AND OPERATIONAL CAPABILITIES FOR CENTRAL CONTROL AND MONITORING BY THE DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE
rows.abstract: The bill directs all government corporations to prepare their respective assets and liability management guideline, to wit: a) financial guidelines to limit borrowing, lending and guaranteeing of any form of financial transaction, and b) operation guidelines to inhibit the corporation from engaging in activities outside their defined capabilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2002-02-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ANY ADVERTISING AGENCY, TELEVISION OR RADIO STATION AND PUBLICATION WHICH EXPLOIT WOMEN AND GLORIFY SEXUAL VIOLENCE IN ITS ADVERTISEMENTS
rows.abstract: The bill imposes on advertising agencies, television or radio stations and publications, which exploit women and glorify sexual violence, a fine of: a) for the 1st offense: P50,000 - P100,000; b) for the 2nd offense: )101,000 - P300,000; and c) for the 3rd offense: P301,000 - P500,000 plus cancellation of license or permit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2005-02-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES AGAINST POLICE OFFICERS, WHO, MALICIOUSLY REFRAIN FROM INSTITUTING PROSECUTION FOR THE PUNISHMENT OF VIOLATORS OF THE LAW OR FOR FAILURE TO TESTIFY IN COURT RESULTING TO THE DISMISSAL OF CASES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 208 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The measure imposes the penalty of prision correccional in its maximum period and perpetual or temporal special disqualification on police officers who maliciously or negligently fail to testify in court resulting to the dismissal of a case.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2005-02-28

rows.author: C001
rows.title_full: AN ACT GOVERNING THE REMITTANCES TO THE PHILIPPINES OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE EARNINGS OF FILIPINO WORKERS ABROAD TO ENSURE THAT THE FOREIGN EXCHANGE EARNINGS OF THESE WORKERS ARE REMITTED THROUGH AUTHORIZED FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS OF THE PHILIPPINE GOVERNMENT OR THEIR AUTHORIZED AGENTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill mandates the remittance of the foreign exchange earnings of overseas Filipino workers to their families, dependents and/or beneficiaries through official financial institutions of the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-02-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING HARBOR PILOTAGE SERVICES AND THE CONDUCT OF HARBOR PILOTS IN ALL PORTS IN THE PHILIPPINES AND RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Pilotage Services Act of 2005.\" The bill seeks to institutionalize the prevailing practices in pilotage services, to rationalize pilotage fees and other charges related to pilotage services, and to define the legal relationship between harbor pilots and pilotage organizations.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-02-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING NOVEMBER TWENTY-FIVE OF EVERY YEAR AS 'NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS DAY FOR THE ELIMINATION OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN
rows.title_short: Declaring Nov. 25 of Every Year as \"National Consciousness Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women\"
rows.abstract: In recognition of the need to establish a comprehensive and structured campaign for national consciousness on anti-violence against women. The bill declares November 25 of every year as the \"National Consciousness Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women\".
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2005-05-10, transmitted to on 2005-05-11 and received by the Senate on 2005-05-17

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to insert the sponsorship speech of Rep. Joson into the Record of the House. Likewise, the Explanatory Note of HB 3783 was adopted as the sponsorship speech of Rep. Maza.

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A MECHANISM FOR AN OPEN SYSTEM OF HIGHER EDUCATION IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: \"Open Tertiary Education Act of 2005.\" The bill seeks to regulate the operation of colleges and universities that offer open and distance education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2005-02-28

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A POSITION OF RURAL DENTIST IN EVERY RURAL HEALTH UNIT UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREF0RE
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to provide a rural dentist in every rural health unit.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2005-02-28

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR BOARD, LODGING AND HOUSING BENEFITS TO EMPLOYEES AND PERSONNEL IN ECOZONE ENTERPRISES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 37 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7916, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE ACT OF 1995\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Ecozone Housing Act.\" The measure seeks to grant board, lodging and/or housing benefits to the employees and personnel of offices located inside economic zones.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-02-28

rows.author: C033
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THREE (3) SMALL FARMERS' REPRESENTATIVES IN THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION (NIA) BOARD BY AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-SIX HUNDRED AND ONE, AS AMENDED, \"AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION\" AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill provides for the inclusion in the Board of Directors of the National Irrigation Administration of 3 representatives from small farmers representing Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE & FOOD since 2005-02-28

rows.author: D024
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE LOCAL EMPLOYMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The measure seeks to establish a local employment authority that shall be responsible for planning and managing the promotion, facilitation, generation and enhancement of employment of local employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-02-28

rows.author: D024
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING THE JURISDICTION OF LABOR CASES BETWEEN THE NATIONAL LABOR RELATION COMMISSION AND THE REGIONAL OFFICES OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE, ARTICLES 129 AND 217 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE FOUR HUNDRED FORTY-TWO (PD 442) AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to grant the Regional Director of the Department of Labor and Employment jurisdiction over labor-related claims \"regardless of the amount of the claim\".
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-02-28

rows.author: D024
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING WORK ARRANGEMENTS BASED ON SECURITY OF TENURE
rows.abstract: \"The Security of Tenure Law of 2005\". The bill seeks to institutionalize the parameters for: a) contracts of employment for an indefinite period, and b) contracts of employment for a definite period. It prescribes the security of tenure, when such contracts are allowed, the form and contents of such contracts and the rights and privileges of employees under contract.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-02-28

rows.author: D024
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A WORKING TIME FLEXIBILIZATION IN THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES, THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLES 83, 85 AND 87 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE FOUR HUNDRED FORTY-TWO (PD 442) AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to modify the existing normal hours of work to allow for a flexible working time or compressed work week scheme.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2005-02-28

rows.author: D024
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE EXCEPTIONS FROM THE NIGHT WORK PROHIBITION OF WOMEN EMPLOYEES, THEREBY AMENDING ARTICLE 131 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE FOUR HUNDRED FORTY-TWO (PD 442), AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: To allow more women to work during nighttime, the bill seeks to lift certain prohibitions identified in Article 131 of the Labor Code, such as: a) in cases of emergencies; b) in case of urgent work performed on machineries, equipment or installation; and c) where work is necessary to prevent serious loss of perishable goods; among others.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05011

rows.author: D053
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PENALIZE DRIVING UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF ALCOHOL AND/OR DANGEROUS DRUGS
rows.abstract: \"Driving Under the Influence Act of 2005.\" The measure penalizes drivers found under the influence of alcohol or dangerours drugs with imprisonment of one year but not more than 2 years or a fine ranging from P20,000 to P80,000, or both. In addition, a 6-month suspension of the license shall be imposed for the 1st conviction, a 12-month suspension for the 2nd conviction and revocation of license and perpetual disqualification to hold a driver's license for the 3rd conviction.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04893

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING ACTS 0F TERRORISM, AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR

It provides for the creation of an Anti-Terrorism Council which shall coordinate, supervise and monitor the government's drive against domestic and international terrorism.
